device.name: Dobot V4 series arm (TCP/IP Python SDK)

facts.text: The SDK is a TCP/IP client: it sends a command string over a socket and reads one text reply per command
A command line is sent with a newline appended and the reply is decoded as UTF-8 and stripped
The dashboard command port is 29999 and the feedback port is 30004
The reply to a command has the form 'ErrorID,{...},Command(...);', for example '0,{[1537,2048]},GetErrorID();'
The error-code table lists 0 as no error and 1537 as the emergency stop triggered
The SDK supports the CRA (CR3A, CR5, CR10, CR16), E6, CRAF and NovaLite families
The README warns to make sure the robot is in a safe position before running
The vendor text requires an easily reachable emergency stop button, a slow speed for the first run and a working range with no people in it
MovJ takes a six-value pose and a coordinate type; with the joint type the pose is six joint angles in degrees and with the Cartesian type six values in millimetres and degrees
The SDK formats every coordinate of a pose with six decimal places before sending it
MovJ and MovL are queue commands: they join the motion queue and are executed in order, unlike the immediate commands such as GetPose and Stop
GetAngle answers with 'ErrorID,{j1,j2,j3,j4,j5,j6},GetAngle();' and GetPose with 'ErrorID,{x,y,z,rx,ry,rz},GetPose();'
GetErrorID answers with 'ErrorID,{[error1,error2,...]},GetErrorID();' and 0 in the error-code table means no error
RobotMode reports 1 initialising, 2 manual, 3 automatic, 4 remote and 9 error
Stop stops the motion command queue the controller was given and any running script
EmergencyStop(mode) presses the emergency stop with mode 1 and releases it with mode 0
The upstream connection class exposes the command exchange as send_receive_text and the connection state as the is_connected property
The upstream SDK requests TCP control mode before it moves: every quick-start example calls RequestControl first
